clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. Sabrina demonstrated a cheerful and cooperative affect, although her attention span was variable, characterized by frequent bouts of distractibility. Upon assessment, her muscle tone was observed to be within normal limits, and she exhibited a typical range of motion for her age. During structured activities, Sabrina required moderate verbal cues to re-engage and maintain task focus. Her fine motor coordination appeared somewhat challenged, particularly in tasks requiring intricate visual-motor integration, where she necessitated hand-over-hand assistance to ensure completion. In self-directed tasks, Sabrina's engagement waned swiftly, prompting maximal redirection. These observations, compounded by the need for frequent cues, significantly influenced the validity of the standardized tests, necessitating adaptations to accurately gauge her abilities and sustain her participation.
